title: Emit region+route labels on streaming disconnect + 5xx error metrics
author: Aisha Bello
description:
Context: Status page transparency upgrades needs better impact classification for partial degradations (streaming-only failures, route/model family-specific 5xx). Today several high-volume error counters are missing consistent region and route attribution, which makes it hard to answer “what’s impacted?” quickly and to map incidents to the new public components. This PR adds standardized region and route labels to selected metrics emitted by the Hosted API serving stack, with guardrails to avoid unbounded cardinality.

What changed: (1) Add `region` label to streaming disconnect counters and selected 5xx counters emitted at the API gateway and serving entrypoints. (2) Add `route` label derived from our internal route taxonomy (chat.completions, responses.stream, embeddings, rerank) with a small fixed allowlist and an `unknown` bucket to prevent explosion. (3) Normalize the label keys and values in one helper so downstream dashboards/alerts can rely on consistent dimensions. (4) Update dashboards/alerts that previously inferred region from hostnames to use the new labels.

Why this approach: We explicitly do NOT label by model_id, customer_id, org_id, deployment_id, or request_path. We only include: `region` (3p stable), `route` (bounded set), and existing dimensions like `http_status` / `error_class`. This keeps cardinality stable while still enabling per-component incident mapping and region-scoped status page updates.

Notes on compatibility: Existing metric names are preserved; we’re adding labels to existing series. Some alert expressions are updated to aggregate across the new dimensions (or to select a route explicitly). Dashboards will show both legacy and labeled breakdowns for 1 week; follow-up will remove the legacy panels after verification.

Example emitted series (illustrative): `redwood_stream_disconnect_total{region="us-east",route="responses.stream",reason="client_disconnect"}` and `redwood_http_requests_total{region="eu-west",route="embeddings",status_code="500"}`.

Testing: unit tests for the route classifier and label injection; integration test validates we emit `region` and `route` for simulated requests; staging smoke verified that series cardinality is within expected bounds and that Prometheus scraping is stable.

Rollout: behind feature flag `metrics.route_region_labels` default OFF; enabled in staging immediately; enable in prod canary (us-east) for 24h, then global. If anything unexpected occurs, flip flag off to revert to unlabeled series behavior.

Related: ENG-4827 status_component tagging support (dashboards will use these labels); ENG-4823 region-level status components; ENG-4828 customer impact classifier helper will consume route/region dimensions for more precise language.
commits: obs: add RouteClassifier with bounded allowlist + tests
api-gateway: plumb region+route into request context and metrics
serving: tag streaming disconnect counters with region+route
alerts/dashboards: update queries to aggregate on new dimensions
config: add metrics.route_region_labels feature flag + docs
review_conversation: Allison Grant: Can we confirm cardinality bounds for `route`? I’m worried about accidental high-card values if someone feeds a raw path. Please document the allowlist and add a fallback bucket so we don’t silently drop metrics.

Aisha Bello (author): Yep. `route` is derived from our internal route taxonomy enum (not path). Added an explicit allowlist mapping + `unknown` fallback, plus a unit test that asserts no raw path strings are permitted. Also added a short comment in the helper about cardinality requirements.
Mina Haddad: For region, are we using the same string values used by status components (us-east/us-west/eu-west)? We should avoid “use1”/“us-east-1” style mixed values.

Aisha Bello (author): Good catch. Normalized to the platform region slug (`us-east`, `us-west`, `eu-west`) via `RegionSlug.fromEnv()`. Updated tests and added a metric validation in the integration test to ensure only these values appear.
Christine Wong: Are we labeling both gateway 5xx and serving 5xx? I want to be able to differentiate gateway-only failures from backend timeouts during incidents.

Aisha Bello (author): This PR labels both but keeps them as separate metric names (`redwood_gateway_http_requests_total` vs `redwood_serving_http_requests_total`). We also keep `error_class` where available (e.g., `upstream_timeout`, `connect_error`). Dashboard panel now shows side-by-side breakdown by route/region.
Miles Thornton: Feature flag path looks good. Can we also ensure the incident-bot can reference these labels for impact summaries later? At least add a note in the metrics doc / naming contract.
Aisha Bello (author): Added a short “consumers” note to the metrics contract comment and linked ENG-4828 in the description. Next PR in the impact classifier will read from the same label keys.
Allison Grant: Approved after changes. Please keep the 1-week dual panels to validate before removing legacy queries.
Christine Wong: Approved. This will help a lot for streaming-only degradations.
post_merge_notes: Enable `metrics.route_region_labels` in staging immediately; prod canary us-east on 2024-07-02 during low-traffic window; watch Prometheus series count + alert noise; update status page comms runbook once dashboards are verified.
